html:
Mari was an ancient city on the Euphrates in eastern Syria, founded around 2900 BCE as a planned trading town between Mesopotamia and the Levant. It was a leading kingdom until 1761 BCE.

Its last king, Zimri-Lim, had a palace of hundreds of rooms with painted walls. In it French archaeologists found about 25,000 clay tablets: letters, contracts and reports that make Mari one of the best documented places of the ancient world. They describe diplomacy, prophets and daily life in the age of Hammurabi of Babylon.

Hammurabi, once Zimri-Lim's ally, conquered Mari and destroyed it. The site was badly looted during the Syrian civil war. See also the Ebla tablets and the Amorites.
sum: Mari was an ancient city on the Euphrates in eastern Syria, founded around 2900 BCE as a planned trading town between Mesopotamia and the Levant. It was a leading kingdom until 1761 BCE.
